approval: Approved by the user on 2026-10-05: Allow this narrow diagnostic. Retain distribution libraries; no suppression or loader workaround.

scope.trigger: Numeric ODBC binding converts ISO-8859-1 to US-ASCII, loading a glibc gconv module. The allocations become unrooted during process shutdown.

root_causes.component: unixODBC configuration cache and installer logging
root_causes.evidence: Upstream explicitly frees these process-global objects in its shared-library destructor fix. Applying those two commits to the exact 2.3.12 sources removes all cache/logging losses in the control; the distribution source retains them until its DSO is unloaded. Repeating 1,000 connection lifetimes adds no allocation sites; the cache expires some entries during that longer run.

Default DontDLClose retains loaded ODBC drivers. GDB stops during glibc __libc_freeres -> __gconv_dl_freemem -> do_release_all -> _dl_close_worker, after application cleanup. After upstream cache cleanup, exactly 120 definite + 298 indirect bytes remain after both 1 and 1,000 Qore connections. Standalone ODBC/iconv without Qore reproduces the preload/list allocation sites (32 definite + 16 indirect bytes) after both 1 and 21 connections; the standalone control does not reproduce every Qore loader root, so the full 418-byte bound also depends on the Qore lifecycle control.

validation: All recorded controls complete successfully. No invalid reads/writes, descriptor losses or possible losses. The distribution Qore control retains 264 definite + 3801 indirect bytes after one connection and 264 + 3462 after 1,000, at the same five allocation contexts.
proposal: Keep the distribution-provided ABI-compatible unixODBC/libltdl packages. Record only these shutdown allocation sites as externally owned qualification diagnostics. The upstream-only patched library is a root-cause control, not a packaged or installed replacement. Experimental loader-cleanup changes are excluded.
exclusions: Any allocation rooted in Qore ODBC code.
Any new allocation site, growing per-connection leak, invalid access or descriptor loss.
PCRE2 JIT is covered by its separately approved evidence record.
No suppression, loader pinning, manual private cache cleanup, or forced unloading of resident drivers.
